mainEntity.name: How much does a Mitsubishi Outlander 2.4 4G69 MIVEC engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A used Mitsubishi Outlander 2.4 4G69 MIVEC engine costs £400-£1,200 supply-only, while a reconditioned unit is £1,200-£2,200 and a full rebuilt engine £2,000-£3,800 [EM-QUOTE]. Fitted costs add £390-£520 labour at a specialist. Compare quotes through EnginesMarket to find the best deal for your exact year and mileage.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of timing belt failure in a Mitsubishi Outlander 2.4 4G69 MIVEC?

acceptedAnswer.text: Symptoms include a squealing or chirping noise from the front of the engine, visible cracking on the belt surface, and engine misfire or rough running. A ticking noise at start-up can indicate a failing hydraulic tensioner. The 4G69's timing belt interval is 105,000 miles or 7 years - many first-generation Outlanders have missed this service, making belt failure more common [THIRD-PARTY][EM-INTERVIEW].

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Mitsubishi Outlander 2.4 4G69 MIVEC?

acceptedAnswer.text: A full rebuilt 4G69 engine costs around £2,000-£3,800 supply-only [EM-QUOTE]. For a 2003-2006 Outlander worth £1,000-£4,500, replacement may represent 50-100% of vehicle value - often not financially sensible. However, if the rest of the car is in excellent condition with low mileage, replacement can extend its life. Always factor in labour (£390-£520) and the value of a 12-month warranty vs. scrapping.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Mitsubishi Outlander 2.4 4G69 MIVEC engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A specialist workshop typically completes a full 4G69 engine swap in 6-8 hours. With parts sourcing and delivery factored in, allow 2-3 days from quote to car back on the road. Supply & fit options through EnginesMarket streamline the process by pairing you with a specialist who has the engine in stock.

mainEntity.name: What Mitsubishi vehicles use the 4G69 engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: The 4G69 2.4-litre MIVEC engine was fitted to multiple Mitsubishi models globally: Outlander (CU0, 2003-2006), Lancer (CS, 2004-2006), Galant (DJ1, 2004-2012), Grandis (NA4, 2003-2011), and Eclipse (4G, 2005-2012) [THIRD-PARTY]. For the Outlander, the 4G69 is specific to first-generation CU0 chassis from 2003-2006 [THIRD-PARTY].

mainEntity.name: Does the Mitsubishi Outlander 2.4 4G69 MIVEC have a timing belt or chain?

acceptedAnswer.text: The Mitsubishi Outlander 2.4 4G69 MIVEC uses a timing belt, not a chain [THIRD-PARTY][EM-INTERVIEW]. This is confirmed by Mitsubishi workshop literature. The belt interval is 105,000 miles or 7 years, and it must be replaced with the tensioner, idler pulleys, and balance shaft belt. The balance shaft belt is often overlooked and can cause engine vibration if not replaced correctly [EM-INTERVIEW].

historyTimeline.h2: Mitsubishi Outlander 2.4 4G69 MIVEC - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The Mitsubishi Outlander 2.4 4G69 MIVEC launched in 2003 as the petrol engine flagship of the first-generation Outlander (CU0 chassis). Powered by the 4G69 2.4-litre SOHC 16-valve engine with MIVEC variable valve timing, it offered 160-165hp and remained the primary petrol choice for UK buyers until the first-generation Outlander was replaced in 2006 [THIRD-PARTY].

milestones.description: 4G69 MIVEC, 2.4-litre, 160hp (119kW) - launch variant with MIVEC variable valve timing and lift, 9.5:1 compression ratio [THIRD-PARTY]
4G69 MIVEC, 2.4-litre, 165hp (123kW) - minor power increase in some markets; UK-spec retained 160hp [THIRD-PARTY]
End of first-generation Outlander (CU0) production; 2.4 4G69 replaced by 2.4 4B12 MIVEC in second-generation models [THIRD-PARTY]

commonProblems.h2: Mitsubishi Outlander 2.4 4G69 MIVEC Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Mitsubishi Outlander 2.4 4G69 MIVEC is a robust SOHC petrol engine, but it has known weak points that can drive replacement decisions: timing belt tensioner wear, MIVEC oil control valve failure, and head gasket issues. Rebuilt engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing these failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Timing Belt & Tensioner Failure - Why the Mitsubishi Outlander 2.4 4G69 MIVEC Timing Belt Wears
problems.rootCause: The 4G69 uses a rubber timing belt with a recommended 105,000-mile / 7-year replacement interval. Many owners miss this service, leading to belt degradation, tensioner hydraulic pressure loss, and potentially catastrophic interference damage if the belt snaps [THIRD-PARTY][EM-INTERVIEW]. The balance shaft belt also requires attention and is often overlooked [EM-INTERVIEW].

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace timing belt, tensioner, idler pulleys, and balance shaft belt
repairOptions.longevity: Routine preventative service; essential every 105,000 miles or 7 years
When timing belt has snapped causing valve/piston damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical 2003-2006 Outlander 2.4 4G69 MIVEC is worth approximately £1,000-£4,500 depending on condition and mileage [THIRD-PARTY][INDUSTRY ESTIMATE]. - Vehicle worth under ~£2,500: replacement likely exceeds vehicle value; consider scrap/part-ex first - Vehicle worth ~£2,500-£5,000: evaluate both; reconditioned is viable if keeping the car 2+ years - Vehicle worth ~£5,000-£8,000: reconditioned/rebuilt usually justifies the premium via warranty and reliability
problems.recommendation: For a 4G69 Outlander approaching 100,000 miles or 7+ years old, preventative timing belt replacement is essential - £350-£550 is far cheaper than a full engine replacement. If the belt has already snapped, a rebuilt engine is often the only viable option [EM-INTERVIEW][THIRD-PARTY].

problems.group: MIVEC Oil Control Valve & Head Gasket Failure
problems.h4: MIVEC Oil Control Valve & Head Gasket Failure - Why the Mitsubishi Outlander 2.4 4G69 MIVEC Suffers Performance Issues
problems.rootCause: The MIVEC system uses an oil control valve (OCV) to switch between low and high cam profiles at ~3,500rpm. OCV failure (fault code P0075) can cause loss of MIVEC function, poor power delivery, and engine pinging [THIRD-PARTY][EM-INTERVIEW]. Head gasket failure between cylinders 3 and 4 has also been reported, causing compression loss and spark knock under acceleration [THIRD-PARTY].

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace oil control valve; basic diagnostic scan required
repairOptions.longevity: First port of call for MIVEC faults; effective if OCV is the only issue

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace head gasket, machine head if warped
repairOptions.longevity: When head gasket failure is confirmed via leakdown test
When head gasket failure has caused overheating damage or warped head

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical 2003-2006 Outlander 2.4 4G69 MIVEC with 100,000+ miles is worth approximately £1,000-£4,000 [THIRD-PARTY][INDUSTRY ESTIMATE].
problems.recommendation: For a 4G69 Outlander with head gasket failure, a leakdown test confirms the issue - be aware that some head bolts may have been under-tightened from factory, causing repeat failures [THIRD-PARTY]. If the vehicle is worth under £2,500 and the head has warped, replacement may not be financially sensible [EM-INTERVIEW].
